facts.text: Functional safety is the part of safety that depends on a control system doing the right thing at the right time, including when its own parts fail.
facts.quote: Functional safety is the part of safety that depends on a control system doing the right thing at the right time, including when its own parts fail.

facts.text: IEC 61508 defines functional safety in terms of correct system responses to inputs, including safe handling of operator errors, hardware failures, software faults and environmental changes.
facts.quote: including safe handling of operator errors, hardware failures, software faults and environmental changes.

facts.text: Functional safety addresses faults rather than whether a healthy camera can see a person in a dust cloud; the latter belongs to safety of the intended functionality.
facts.quote: It is not about whether a healthy camera can see a person in a dust cloud; that belongs to the safety of the intended functionality

facts.text: The framework for a brake-commanding function on earth-moving machines is ISO 19014, not ISO 26262.
facts.quote: The framework for a brake-commanding function on earth-moving machines is ISO 19014, not ISO 26262

facts.text: ISO 15998, the earlier standard for the earth-moving machine control-system framework, was withdrawn in 2022.
facts.quote: the earlier ISO 15998 was withdrawn in 2022 [Chapter 3]

facts.text: The ISO 19014 lifecycle starts with hazard and risk analysis and determination of the required Machine Performance Level using Part 1 or the Part 5 tables.
facts.quote: hazard and risk analysis and the required Machine Performance Level (Part 1, or the Part 5 tables)

facts.text: ISO 19014 Part 2 addresses architecture and fault behavior that give the achieved Machine Performance Level.
facts.quote: architecture and fault behavior giving the achieved level (Part 2)

facts.text: ISO 19014 Part 3 addresses environmental qualification of the electronics.
ISO 19014 Part 4 addresses software and data transmission.
The earth-moving machine functional-safety lifecycle includes brake capability under ISO 3450.
All five parts of ISO 19014 were due to be reissued in October 2026, a few months before design verification is frozen.
facts.quote: All five parts were due to be reissued in October 2026, a few months before design verification is frozen

facts.text: The program plan should baseline the ISO 19014 editions actually published rather than assume the planned October 2026 reissues are available.
facts.quote: so the plan should baseline the editions actually published [Chapter 3]

facts.text: ISO 19014 does not assume that every brake demand is safe, so the unsafe-intervention function needs its own analysis.
facts.quote: ISO 19014 does not assume that every brake demand is safe, which is why the unsafe-intervention function gets its own analysis [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Much functional-safety evidence is analytical—hazard analysis, architecture assessment, software verification and fault reasoning—so analysis and simulation fit naturally within functional safety.
facts.quote: Much functional-safety evidence is analytical (hazard analysis, architecture assessment, software verification, fault reasoning), so analysis and simulation sit naturally inside it

facts.text: No off-road rule allows simulation to replace a prescribed physical test.
facts.quote: no off-road rule lets simulation replace a prescribed physical test [Chapter 3]

facts.text: The functional safety engineer in the booklet's hostile review objects that the program treats a new safety-control function as an incremental feature.
facts.quote: The functional safety engineer in the booklet's hostile review objects that the program treats a new safety-control function as an incremental feature.

facts.text: The program should have an approved Machine Control System Safety Analysis before the prototype arrives, covering failure to intervene and incorrect intervention, allocated performance levels, and traceability from each requirement to its test.
facts.quote: an approved Machine Control System Safety Analysis before the prototype arrives, with requirements for both failure to intervene and incorrect intervention, allocated performance levels, and traceability from each requirement to its test [Chapter 13]
